about.text: A creamy, jelly-like milk dessert of northern Spain, especially Navarre and the Basque Country: warm milk set with rennet and eaten with sugar or honey. It was traditionally made with sheep's milk in a clay or wooden bowl; today it is mostly cow's milk.

facts.v: Traditionally a clay or wooden bowl (kaiku), in the Basque Country warmed with a red-hot poker, which gave a faint burnt taste
Cundiboyacense highland: cow-milk cuajada with melado (panela syrup)
Served as a dessert with honey and walnuts or sugar, or for breakfast with fruit
